claims.claim: Caterpillar links power-generation equipment and industrial machines to the infrastructure needed for compute, construction and resource extraction; the 2-GW AI-power order creates a direct bridge from gas generation to hyperscale compute availability, while the FieldAI collaboration targets the labor/productivity bottleneck through autonomy and physical AI.

The causal chain is not self-sufficient: gas supply, permitting, grid/interconnection choices, emissions constraints, commissioning and customer utilization remain successor bottlenecks, while autonomy benefits depend on safe deployment and workflow integration.

causalEdges: generator sets -> dedicated power -> data-center compute availability -> AI/digital services
physical AI/autonomy -> machine productivity/safety -> infrastructure/resource throughput
fuel/permitting/commissioning -> usable generation -> realized compute capacity

risks.risk: Dedicated gas generation can relieve grid timing constraints while creating fuel, emissions and permitting dependencies.

unknowns.unknown: The disclosed order does not quantify revenue, margin or commissioning performance.

claims.claim: The 2-GW order is a concrete execution checkpoint, but order size in watts should not be conflated with recognized revenue, margin or durable demand; delivery and commissioning remain necessary falsification tests.
FieldAI collaboration supports optionality in autonomy but does not yet establish scaled commercial economics in the cited evidence.

causalEdges: order -> delivery/commissioning -> recognized economics -> thesis validation

risks.risk: AI infrastructure demand may be lumpy; alternative power architectures can substitute for gas generator sets.
Natural-gas price, availability, permitting and emissions policy can reduce project economics or timing.
Autonomy partnership announcements can create confidence inflation before deployment economics are demonstrated.

unknowns.unknown: Company-wide current execution and order profitability remain for Alpha underwriting because Scout did not retrieve current Q2 company-wide evidence.
